*   **Memory Complexity:** It requires no additional storage for neighborhood data, unlike CM which needs neighboring points [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the Householder (HH) technique 'only requires the three components of the normal vector to compute the tangent and bitangent vectors' and that calculations are performed in the geometry shader 'to avoid storing three extra vertices per point'. In contrast, it notes that the Covariance Matrix (CM) technique 'takes the neighboring points as input to define splat orientation.' This confirms that HH requires no additional storage for neighborhood data, whereas CM does.

Therefore, the claim accurately reflects the conditions and trade-offs described in the evidence.
